requirements.quote: For this to be effective, endpoints need to ensure that connection IDs they provide cannot be linked by any other entity.
requirements.condition: When providing connection IDs intended to prevent correlation across network paths.
requirements.required_behavior: Ensure that the provided connection IDs cannot be linked by an entity other than the peer.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Provide connection IDs that another entity can link to one another.
requirements.why_checkable: The security objective is stated, but the chunk provides no concrete algorithm or observable criterion for deciding whether arbitrary connection IDs are linkable by another entity.

requirements.quote: At any time, endpoints MAY change the Destination Connection ID they transmit with to a value that has not been used on another path.
requirements.condition: At any time, when selecting a Destination Connection ID for transmission.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the endpoint to change to a Destination Connection ID value that has not been used on another path.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can track connection ID use by path and verify that changing to an unused-on-other-path value is accepted.

requirements.quote: An endpoint MUST NOT reuse a connection ID when sending from more than one local address
requirements.condition: When an endpoint sends packets from multiple local addresses.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reuse the same connection ID for packets sent from more than one local address.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet traces can associate each transmitted connection ID with its local source address and detect reuse across addresses.

requirements.quote: An endpoint MUST NOT reuse a connection ID when sending from more than one local address -- for example, when initiating connection migration as described in Section 9.2 or when probing a new network path as described in Section 9.1.
requirements.condition: When initiating connection migration or probing a new network path from a different local address.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reuse a connection ID that was used while sending from another local address.
requirements.why_checkable: The explicit examples apply the preceding prohibition to two observable path-changing operations.

requirements.quote: Similarly, an endpoint MUST NOT reuse a connection ID when sending to more than one destination address.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint sends packets to multiple destination addresses.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reuse the same connection ID for packets sent to more than one destination address.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet traces can associate each transmitted connection ID with its destination address and detect reuse across destinations.

requirements.quote: Due to network changes outside the control of its peer, an endpoint might receive packets from a new source address with the same Destination Connection ID field value, in which case it MAY continue to use the current connection ID with the new remote address while still sending from the same local address.
requirements.condition: When network changes outside the peer's control cause packets with the same Destination Connection ID to arrive from a new source address, and the endpoint continues sending from the same local address.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the endpoint to continue using its current connection ID with the new remote address.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can change the peer's source address while preserving the Destination Connection ID and local sending address, then verify that continued use of the current connection ID is accepted.

requirements.quote: These requirements regarding connection ID reuse apply only to the sending of packets, as unintentional changes in path without a change in connection ID are possible.
requirements.condition: When applying the connection ID reuse requirements in this section.
requirements.required_behavior: Apply the reuse restrictions to the endpoint's sending of packets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Treat an unintentional received-path change without a connection ID change as itself violating these sending restrictions.
requirements.why_checkable: The statement defines the operational scope of the reuse checks and distinguishes transmitted behavior from unintentional path changes.

requirements.quote: Using different connection IDs for packets sent in both directions on each new network path eliminates the use of the connection ID for linking packets from the same connection across different network paths.
requirements.condition: For packets sent in both directions on each new network path, when preventing connection-ID-based cross-path linkage.
requirements.required_behavior: Use connection IDs that differ across the network paths in both sending directions.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use a connection ID in a way that links packets from the same connection across different network paths.
requirements.why_checkable: A bidirectional packet trace can compare connection IDs across paths, although the sentence expresses a security consequence rather than a normative implementation requirement.

requirements.quote: Header protection ensures that packet numbers cannot be used to correlate activity.
requirements.condition: When packet numbers are exposed to passive observation.
requirements.required_behavior: Apply header protection so packet numbers cannot be used to correlate activity.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Expose packet numbers in a form usable for activity correlation.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation test can inspect protected packet headers and determine whether packet numbers are observable, though this sentence primarily states a security property.

requirements.quote: This does not prevent other properties of packets, such as timing and size, from being used to correlate activity.
requirements.condition: When connection IDs differ across paths and packet numbers are protected.
requirements.why_checkable: The sentence identifies residual correlation channels but does not constrain any implementation behavior concerning them.

requirements.quote: An endpoint SHOULD NOT initiate migration with a peer that has requested a zero-length connection ID, because traffic over the new path might be trivially linkable to traffic over the old one.
requirements.condition: When the peer has requested a zero-length connection ID.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Initiate connection migration with that peer, absent a justified exception to the SHOULD NOT requirement.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can configure a peer to request a zero-length connection ID and observe whether the endpoint initiates migration.

requirements.quote: If the server is able to associate packets with a zero-length connection ID to the right connection, it means that the server is using other information to demultiplex packets.
requirements.condition: When a server associates a packet carrying a zero-length connection ID with the correct connection.
requirements.required_behavior: Use information other than the connection ID to demultiplex that packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Claim to demultiplex solely by the zero-length connection ID.
requirements.why_checkable: Server instrumentation can identify which packet attributes or routing context are used to select the connection.

requirements.quote: Information that might allow correct routing of packets across multiple network paths will also allow activity on those paths to be linked by entities other than the peer.
requirements.condition: When information enables correct routing across multiple network paths.
requirements.why_checkable: This is a security observation, but it does not prescribe a concrete behavior and uses the uncertain phrase 'might allow' for the routing premise.

requirements.quote: A client might wish to reduce linkability by switching to a new connection ID, source UDP port, or IP address (see [RFC8981]) when sending traffic after a period of inactivity.
requirements.condition: When a client resumes sending traffic after a period of inactivity and wishes to reduce linkability.
requirements.required_behavior: Switch to a new connection ID, source UDP port, or IP address.
requirements.why_checkable: The alternatives are observable, but 'might wish' is explanatory rather than a requirement or defined permission.

requirements.quote: Changing the address from which it sends packets at the same time might cause the server to detect a connection migration.
requirements.condition: When a client changes its sending address while resuming traffic.
requirements.why_checkable: The statement describes only a possible server reaction and does not require migration detection in a defined circumstance.

requirements.quote: Changing address can cause a peer to reset its congestion control state (see Section 9.4), so addresses SHOULD only be changed infrequently.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint is considering changing its sending address.
requirements.why_checkable: The term 'infrequently' has no quantitative threshold in this chunk, so conformance cannot be determined objectively.

requirements.quote: An endpoint that exhausts available connection IDs cannot probe new paths or initiate migration, nor can it respond to probes or attempts by its peer to migrate.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint has exhausted its available connection IDs.
requirements.why_checkable: A state-machine test can exhaust the connection ID pool and attempt to start path probing.

requirements.quote: An endpoint that exhausts available connection IDs cannot probe new paths or initiate migration, nor can it respond to probes or attempts by its peer to migrate.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint has exhausted its available connection IDs.
requirements.why_checkable: A state-machine test can exhaust the connection ID pool and attempt locally initiated migration.

requirements.quote: An endpoint that exhausts available connection IDs cannot probe new paths or initiate migration, nor can it respond to probes or attempts by its peer to migrate.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint has exhausted its available connection IDs and receives a peer probe.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Respond to the peer's probe using a new path.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can exhaust available connection IDs, deliver a peer path probe, and observe whether the endpoint responds.

requirements.quote: An endpoint that exhausts available connection IDs cannot probe new paths or initiate migration, nor can it respond to probes or attempts by its peer to migrate.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint has exhausted its available connection IDs and its peer attempts to migrate.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Respond to the peer's migration attempt using a new path.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can exhaust available connection IDs, cause the peer to attempt migration, and observe the endpoint's response.

requirements.quote: To ensure that migration is possible and packets sent on different paths cannot be correlated, endpoints SHOULD provide new connection IDs before peers migrate; see Section 5.1.1.
requirements.condition: Before a peer migrates.
requirements.required_behavior: Provide new connection IDs to the peer so migration remains possible and different paths need not reuse identifiers.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Withhold new connection IDs until the peer has no identifiers available for migration, absent a justified exception to the SHOULD requirement.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can inspect whether new connection IDs are supplied before peer migration and whether the peer retains an available identifier.

requirements.quote: If a peer might have exhausted available connection IDs, a migrating endpoint could include a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame in all packets sent on a new network path.
requirements.condition: When a migrating endpoint believes its peer might have exhausted available connection IDs and sends packets on a new network path.
requirements.required_behavior: Include a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame in every packet sent on the new path.
requirements.why_checkable: Frame presence in every new-path packet is observable, but 'could include' presents a non-normative possibility rather than a required or clearly granted behavior.
